grade.basis: Complete 24-bar G-major prelude assessed from all four individual parts (PDF pp.5–8), not its fugue or the piano original. Cello 1 sets the ceiling: persistent upper-register ledger-line reading, chromatic semiquaver sequences, changing two-note slurs/detached and lifted attacks, ornament and register changes; cello 2/3 also receive active semiquaver material. Quarter=56 keeps the fastest notation manageable; short duration and single-note writing limit stamina/coordination demand. Early advanced (level 4, roughly ABRSM 7/RCM 8), advisory within one level; no ensemble uplift.

findings.finding: 952243.pdf: complete individual parts inspected; cello 1 opening and bars 12–24 carry upper-register semiquavers and mixed articulation; cello 4 switches arco/pizzicato but does not exceed the first-part ceiling.

grade.basis: Complete 24-bar C-minor prelude assessed from all four individual parts (PDF pp.5–8); the separately arranged fugue is excluded. Cello 1 combines substantial upper ledger-line writing and treble/bass clef changes, chromatic motion, repeated retaken attacks, sustained tones, and eighth/sixteenth subdivisions; cello 4 adds low-register string crossings and occasional double notes. Explicit Adagio eighth=80 makes the busy-looking surface slow in execution. Upper-position intonation and controlled sustained sound support early advanced level 4 rather than a grade inherited from WTC piano; approximately one-level advisory tolerance.

findings.finding: 957315.pdf: Adagio eighth=80, 4/4, three-flat C-minor arrangement; all four complete parts inspected. First-part clef/register changes and exposed lyrical continuity set the ceiling; bass-part rhythmic activity is not a fast virtuoso passage.

grade.basis: Complete 24-bar F-major prelude assessed from all four individual parts (PDF pp.1–5), with the full score available on pp.6–9. Cello 1 sets a higher ceiling through recurrent semiquaver runs, wide register changes, treble/tenor/bass clef reading, chromatic alterations and a trill, with exposed upper-register entries and short slurs amid detached notes. Cello 2 also has clef changes and agile runs, while cello 4 carries substantial continuous semiquaver material. Joyously implies buoyant motion, although no numerical tempo is supplied; the short span and absence of sustained double-stop work restrain the estimate. Level 5 advanced, with medium confidence and about one-level tolerance rather than exhaustive fingering certification.

findings.finding: 957296.pdf: complete first part spans pp.1–2; parts 2–4 follow on pp.3–5. The Joyously marking, semiquaver figuration, accidentals, changing clefs and brief arco/pizzicato changes were checked across the complete prelude.

grade.basis: Whole six-cello Pizzicato-Polka reviewed through the complete score, PDF pp.3–10 (bars 1–110), with separate parts supplied afterward. Cello 1 sets the ceiling through upper-register melody, bass/tenor/treble clef changes, semiquaver bursts, leaps and chromatic lines; other parts contain repeated eighth-note accompaniment, exchanged melody and plucked double/triple stops. Entirely pizzicato: clean repeated plucks, quick string changes and balanced chords replace bow technique as the challenge. Short dance sections and rests keep stamina bounded, despite 110 bars. No metronome marking observed; lively polka character assumed for the advisory estimate. Level 4 early advanced, about one-level tolerance; six players do not automatically raise the grade.

findings.finding: 451336.pdf: full score pp.3–10 covers opening, trio, return and coda through final bar 110; pizzicato is marked at the opening. Upper melody/clef changes and chordal plucks in multiple lower parts checked across the whole arrangement. Score title credits only J Strauss Jr; factual co-composer attribution is outside this musical grade.
